ref_extractions.title: Age and sex modulate the variability of neural responses to naturalistic videos
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This 2017 bioRxiv paper studies EEG inter-subject correlation during video watching in a developmental sample but uses earlier HBN data collection (pre-release), not the specific ds005505 BIDS-formatted EEG release from 2025. It is related research from the HBN consortium but not an analysis of the specific dataset in question.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Authors include HBN researchers (Petroni, Cohen, Ai, Langer, Henin, Vanderwal, Milham, Parra) studying naturalistic video responses, but using a different/earlier data collection phase than the ds005505 BIDS release.

ref_extractions.title: HBN-EEG: The FAIR implementation of the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) electroencephalography dataset
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the primary data descriptor paper for the HBN-EEG dataset. It explicitly describes and references OpenNeuro ds005505 (one of nine dataset releases) and details the six tasks, BIDS formatting, HED annotations, and participant metadata. The paper defines the dataset structure that supports ML classification/regression tasks.
ref_extractions.paradigm: multi-task (resting, video, contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search, surround suppression)
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Events annotated using HED schema; task events include contrastTrial_start, buttonPress, video_start/stop, fixpoint_ON; sessions include passive and active task epochs
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Four psychopathology dimensions: internalizing, externalizing, attention, p-factor; demographic: age, gender
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: HED-annotated events enable machine learning across tasks; super-meta includes behavioral response accuracy and timing
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Paper explicitly lists https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds005505 as one of nine releases; describes 6 tasks (3 passive, 3 active) with detailed event markers and BIDS formatting suitable for ML pipelines.

ref_extractions.title: An open resource for transdiagnostic research in pediatric mental health and learning disorders
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This Scientific Data paper describes the original HBN Biobank initiative and its first data release (n=664), predating the specific ds005505 EEG release. It describes the multi-modal design including EEG but does not focus on EEG methodology. It is background/context for the dataset.
ref_extractions.paradigm: multi-modal biobank (includes EEG, fMRI, eye tracking, behavioral)
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: This paper describes the HBN initiative design; the specific EEG tasks are detailed in later papers
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: HBN Biobank rationale and protocol; first release n=664; includes EEG but not specific to ds005505 BIDS release.

ref_extractions.title: A resource for assessing information processing in the developing brain using EEG and eye tracking
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This Scientific Data paper (2017) describes the EEG paradigm battery that directly informed the HBN EEG protocol. It uses 126 subjects from the CMI practice and describes the six tasks (resting, surround suppression, videos, contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search) that match ds005505. However, this is a separate pilot dataset (n=126, ages 6-44), not the ds005505 release.
ref_extractions.paradigm: six-task battery: resting-state, surround suppression, video watching, contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Active tasks require button press responses; passive tasks include movie watching and resting
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Clinical diagnosis categories; cognitive test battery scores
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Pilot/feasibility study that defined the HBN EEG paradigm battery
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Describes the paradigm battery (6 tasks) that directly corresponds to ds005505 tasks; uses earlier/pilot data (n=126) not the specific ds005505 release.

ref_extractions.title: HBN-EEG: The FAIR implementation of the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) electroencephalography dataset
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: PDF version of the HBN-EEG data descriptor paper. Explicitly describes the dataset including ds005505 release, BIDS formatting, HED annotations for events, and the six-task paradigm. Defines the data structure and participant metadata available for ML tasks.
ref_extractions.paradigm: six-task battery (resting state, surround suppression, movie watching, contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search)
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Events annotated with HED schema; includes task-condition events, behavioral responses, environmental context; 128-channel EEG at 500Hz
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Age, gender, four psychopathology dimensions (internalizing, externalizing, attention, p-factor) from bifactor model
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Super-meta includes HED-annotated events enabling mega-analysis and cross-dataset ML; behavioral and task-condition annotations in BIDS format
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Detailed methodology for ds005505: 2639 participants across 9 releases, BIDS format, HED annotations, six tasks with detailed event markers and psychopathology factors.

ref_extractions.title: Automagic: Standardized preprocessing of big EEG data
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This NeuroImage paper describes Automagic, an EEG preprocessing toolbox. It mentions HBN as a large-scale initiative that includes EEG, but does not use or analyze the specific ds005505 dataset. The paper focuses on preprocessing methodology, not dataset-specific analysis.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: HBN is mentioned as context/example of large-scale EEG initiative; paper focuses on Automagic preprocessing software, not analysis of HBN EEG data.

ref_extractions.title: Functional connectivity of EEG is subject-specific, associated with phenotype, and different from fMRI
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This NeuroImage paper analyzes EEG functional connectivity (phase-coupling using imaginary coherence) from the HBN Biobank (1657 individuals, ages 5-21) and associates connectivity patterns with phenotypes (age, sex, IQ, ADHD, socioeconomic status, anxiety). It uses resting-state EEG and video-watching tasks, directly relevant to ds005505 paradigms.
ref_extractions.paradigm: resting-state EEG, video watching, visual flicker
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Long-duration connectivity epochs; analyzed phase-coupling across frequency bands (imaginary coherence iCOH)
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Age, sex, IQ, ADHD measures, socioeconomic status, anxiety, Child Behavior Checklist Score; phenotypic measures including attention
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Raw EEG analyzed for functional connectivity; phenotype associations tested across multiple behavioral/demographic measures
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Explicitly uses HBN Biobank EEG data; association analysis with phenotypic variables; defines regression task linking EEG connectivity to demographics and clinical measures.

ref_extractions.title: A benchmark for prediction of psychiatric multimorbidity from resting EEG data in a large pediatric sample
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This NeuroImage paper describes an ML benchmark challenge using HBN resting-state EEG to predict psychiatric multimorbidity. It explicitly uses HBN data (N=2042) and defines concrete ML tasks: multi-task multi-label classification of 7 DSM-V diagnoses and regression for symptom severity. The paper is specifically about using HBN EEG for predictive classification.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Resting-state EEG epochs for feature extraction; connectivity and spectral features; multi-task prediction
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Seven DSM-V psychiatric diagnoses (multi-label): multi-task classification; psychiatric symptom severity dimensions for regression
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Defines specific ML benchmark with hidden test sets; participant-level labels from clinical assessments; super-meta includes psychopathology factor scores
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Explicit ML benchmark using HBN EEG; defines multi-label classification task for 7 psychiatric diagnoses plus dimensional symptom severity regression. This is a direct ML application of the HBN EEG dataset.

ref_extractions.title: A resource for assessing information processing in the developing brain using EEG and eye tracking
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: PDF version of the 2017 Scientific Data paper describing the EEG paradigm battery. This paper describes the six-task design (resting, surround suppression, videos, contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search) that directly corresponds to ds005505 paradigms. However, it uses a separate pilot dataset (n=126) from the CMI practice, not the specific ds005505 release.
ref_extractions.paradigm: six-task battery: resting-state, surround suppression, video watching, contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Active tasks with button press responses; passive tasks including naturalistic video; concurrent eye tracking
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Clinical diagnosis categories; cognitive test battery scores; psychiatric functioning measures
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Pilot study defining the paradigm battery that informed HBN EEG protocol; super-meta includes behavioral and eye tracking data
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Paradigm battery (n=126) directly corresponds to ds005505 tasks; this is the feasibility/pilot study preceding the larger HBN EEG release.

feasibility_reason: The dataset has rich phenotypic measures (p_factor, attention, internalizing, externalizing, age) and well-structured event markers across six behavioral paradigms, with multiple relevant references demonstrating direct ML applications on HBN EEG data for both classification (7 psychiatric labels) and regression (dimensional symptom severity) tasks.
tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Contrast Detection ERP

**Task Type**: Event-Related Potential (ERP) / Sensory Discrimination
**Epoch Method**: epoch_by_event_hdf5
**Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s
**Label Route**: event
**Meta Level**: raw

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| contrast:contrastTrial_start | 0 | Contrast change trial onset (baseline) |
| contrast:left_target | 1 | Left-side leaning target stimulus |
| contrast:right_target | 2 | Right-side leaning target stimulus |
| contrast:left_buttonPress | 1 | Left-hand response to left target |
| contrast:right_buttonPress | 2 | Right-hand response to right target |

**Evidence (DOI)**: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 (HBN-EEG dataset paper); 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2022.119348 (psychiatric multimorbidity benchmark)

**Kernel Notes**: 8829 contrastTrial_start events with ~4243 left and ~4231 right targets enable correct vs incorrect response classification. Block markers (contrastChangeB1/B2/B3_start) indicate run boundaries. Orphan events (contrastTrial_start without 'contrast:' prefix) should be prefixed for consistent epoching. Epoching on contrastTrial_start captures pre-stimulus baseline and post-stimulus discrimination response.

---

### Classical Task 2: Resting-State Psychopathology Classification

**Task Type**: Classification / Regression (Clinical)
**Epoch Method**: epoch_by_long_event_hdf5
**Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = segment_length (4–10 s), overlap = 0.0–0.5
**Label Route**: misc
**Meta Level**: super

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| resting:instructed_toOpenEyes | eyes_open | Eye-open resting state period |
| resting:instructed_toCloseEyes | eyes_closed | Eye-closed resting state period |
| resting:resting_start | 1 | Resting state block initiation |

**Evidence (DOI)**: 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2022.119348 (7-class DSM-V psychiatric prediction benchmark); 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2020.117001 (resting EEG phenotype associations); 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 (HBN-EEG dataset)

**Kernel Notes**: Super-meta labels from participants.tsv include p_factor, attention, internalizing, externalizing. Kernel must load per-subject labels from companion phenotype file. 680 eye-close and 816 eye-open instruction events enable state comparison. Orphan sequence learning events in resting files indicate file concatenation errors; filter to resting state-specific events only. Age range 5.2–21.7 years requires age-appropriate normative comparisons.

---

### Classical Task 3: Movie Watching Connectivity

**Task Type**: Naturalistic Paradigm / Connectivity Analysis
**Epoch Method**: epoch_by_long_event_hdf5
**Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = video_duration (30–120 s)
**Label Route**: stim
**Meta Level**: raw

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| video_start | 1 | Movie clip onset |
| video_stop | 0 | Movie clip offset |
| contrast:video_start | 1 | Contrast task video onset (block) |
| contrast:video_stop | 0 | Contrast task video offset |
| resting:video_start | 1 | Resting file video event (orphan) |
| resting:video_stop | 0 | Resting file video event (orphan) |

**Evidence (DOI)**: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261; 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2020.117001 (functional connectivity during video viewing)

**Kernel Notes**: Four movies (DespicableMe, DiaryOfAWimpyKid, FunwithFractals, ThePresent) with 624 video_start events. Long-epoch method captures sustained processing and connectivity changes. HED schema annotates 24 fps playback parameters. Parent-review of clips documented in paradigm notes.

---

### Classical Task 4: Psychiatric Multimorbidity Prediction

**Task Type**: Multi-Label Classification / Regression (Clinical)
**Epoch Method**: epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5
**Epoch Parameters**: segment_length = 4–10 s, overlap = 0.0–0.5
**Label Route**: misc
**Meta Level**: super

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| resting:instructed_toOpenEyes | eyes_open_segment | Eye-open resting segment |
| resting:instructed_toCloseEyes | eyes_closed_segment | Eye-closed resting segment |

**Super-Meta Label Mapping**:
| Phenotype Field | Type | Description |
|-----------------|------|-------------|
| p_factor | Regression | General psychopathology bifactor |
| attention | Regression | Attention dimension score |
| internalizing | Regression | Internalizing symptoms |
| externalizing | Regression | Externalizing symptoms |
| DSM-V categories (binary) | Classification | Multi-label psychiatric diagnoses |

**Evidence (DOI)**: 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2022.119348 (explicit 7-class benchmark); 10.1038/sdata.2017.40 (HBN paradigm battery)

**Kernel Notes**: This is the direct ML benchmark task. Participants.tsv contains continuous (p_factor, attention, internalizing, externalizing) and binary (DSM-V) labels. Kernel must extract super-meta from companion phenotype files. Segment-level predictions aggregated at subject level. Age/sex included as covariates.

---

### Normal Task 1: Sequence Learning

**Task Type**: Cognitive / Motor Sequence Learning
**Epoch Method**: epoch_by_event_hdf5
**Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.8 s
**Label Route**: event
**Meta Level**: raw

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| seqLearning:seqLearning_start | 1 | Sequence learning block onset |
| seqLearning:learningBlock_1–5 | block_n | Learning block structure markers |
| seqLearning:dot_no1_ON | 1 | Dot 1 stimulus onset (6-target version) |
| seqLearning:dot_no7_ON | 7 | Dot 7 stimulus onset (8-target version) |
| seqLearning:dot_no8_ON | 8 | Dot 8 stimulus onset (8-target version) |
| dot_no2_ON | 2 | Orphan dot stimulus (resting file) |
| dot_no3_ON | 3 | Orphan dot stimulus (resting file) |

**Evidence (DOI)**: 10.1038/sdata.2017.40 (paradigm battery defining sequence learning); 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 (dataset documentation)

**Kernel Notes**: 118 runs with 5 learning blocks each; dots 1-8 (ON/OFF pairs) mark visual sequence positions. 6-target (590 dot_ON events) and 8-target (780-783 dot_ON events) variants exist. Orphan dot events in resting files indicate cross-task contamination. Epoch on dot_ON captures stimulus-locked sequential learning responses.

---

### Normal Task 2: Surround Suppression

**Task Type**: Visual Sensory / Contrast Processing
**Epoch Method**: epoch_by_event_hdf5
**Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.6 s
**Label Route**: event
**Meta Level**: raw

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| fixpoint_ON | 0 | Fixation point onset (baseline) |
| stim_ON | 1 | Peripheral disk stimulation onset |
| surroundSuppB1_start | block_1 | Surround suppression block 1 start |
| surroundSuppB2_start | block_2 | Surround suppression block 2 start |

**Evidence (DOI)**: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261; 10.1038/sdata.2017.40

**Kernel Notes**: 13248 fixpoint_ON and 13278 stim_ON events enable stimulus vs baseline comparison. B1/B2 block markers indicate run structure (108 and 99 starts). HED schema annotates background presence (sinusoidal gratings) and luminance contrast conditions. Epoch on stim_ON captures visual response with and without surround suppression.

---

### Potential Task 1: Symbol Search Cognitive Processing

**Task Type**: Cognitive / Visual Search
**Epoch Method**: epoch_by_event_hdf5
**Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.8 s
**Label Route**: event
**Meta Level**: raw

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| symbolSearch_start | 1 | Symbol search task initiation |
| newPage | 0 | New search query page onset |
| trialResponse | response_value | Subject response (0=false, 1=true) |

**Evidence (DOI)**: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 (dataset paper); paradigm plausible from battery description (10.1038/sdata.2017.40)

**Kernel Notes**: 76 runs, 194 newPage events, 1247 trialResponse events. Event code 14 indicates response; user_answer and correct_answer in events.json enable accuracy computation. New page onset marks cognitive search initiation. Participant availability in participants.tsv varies (available/unavailable/caution).

---

### Potential Task 2: Block-Level Contrast Discrimination

**Task Type**: Block-Level Sensory Discrimination
**Epoch Method**: epoch_by_event_hdf5
**Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.5 s, tmax = 3.0 s
**Label Route**: event
**Meta Level**: raw

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| contrast:contrastChangeB1_start | block_1 | Contrast change block 1 onset |
| contrast:contrastChangeB2_start | block_2 | Contrast change block 2 onset |
| contrast:contrastChangeB3_start | block_3 | Contrast change block 3 onset |
| contrastChangeB2_start | block_2_orphan | Orphan block 2 marker |
| contrastChangeB3_start | block_3_orphan | Orphan block 3 marker |

**Evidence (DOI)**: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261; paradigm described in 10.1038/sdata.2017.40

**Kernel Notes**: Block-level analysis captures sustained attention and adaptation effects. Orphan events (6 B2, 1 B3 without 'contrast:' prefix) indicate annotation inconsistency. 102, 111, 142 block start counts across B1/B2/B3 support block-level response averaging.
